Each key is the spelling a script writes (`request.security("SP:SPX", …)`; a seed as `request.seed(source, symbol, …)` spells `<SOURCE>:<SYMBOL>`, upper-cased). `store` is the key our bars route serves it under (`/api/bars/<store>`), `timeframes` the chart timeframes the witness covers, `queue_row` / `probe` the capture that settles it, `alignment` how the witness places the series' bars on a chart's bars (`otherSymbols.js::WITNESS_ALIGNMENTS`). ⛔ A ROW SERVES ONLY WHEN IT CARRIES `witness` (the capture) AND `captured` (its date) — the rule `symbolScope.json::confirmed` keeps: a row without a witness is an assertion wearing a data structure. Without them the spelling is refused BY NAME, citing its queue row (`otherSymbols.js::staticallyUnservable`, the one gate both lanes ask). Turning a row on is ONE data edit. ⭐ The `seed` rows are the frontend's manifest of `api/services/pine_seed_store.py::SEEDS`; `tests/test_pine_seed_manifest.py` rails that the two agree. ⭐⭐ RS RATING L11 (2026-11-17) — a chart timeframe with a block of its own (`periods.<tf>`) is served from the series HELD at another timeframe (`held`; fetched and cached under `<store>@<held>`, `otherSymbols.js::heldFetchOf`) and read per request timeframe as its capture witnessed (`reads`: `period` = the chart's own timeframe, a FOLD; `D` = a daily read below the chart, the row's daily read SAMPLED per chart bar; `otherSymbols.js::WITNESS_PERIOD_READS`). A block serves only with its own `witness` + `captured`; a timeframe listed in `timeframes` with no block is the row's own (`alignment`).
